The [[premier of Prince Edward Island]] is the [[first minister]] for the [[Provinces and territories of Canada|Canadian province]] of [[Prince Edward Island]]. They are the province's [[head of government]] and ''de facto'' chief executive.

[[Prince Edward Island]] was a British [[crown colony]] before it joined [[Canadian Confederation]] in 1873. It has had a system of [[responsible government]] since 1851, and the province kept its own legislature to deal with provincial matters after joining Confederation.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=November 9, 2008|url=http://www.elections.ca/content.asp?section=gen&document=chap1&dir=his&lang=e&textonly=false|title=A History of the Vote in Canada |publisher=Elections Canada }}</ref> Prince Edward Island has a unicameral [[Westminster System|Westminster-style]] [[parliamentary government]], in which the premier is the leader of the party that controls the most seats in the [[Legislative Assembly of Prince Edward Island|Legislative Assembly]].<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |access-date=November 9, 2008 |url=https://www.thecanadianencyclopedia.ca/en/article/provincial-government |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091121011558/http://www.thecanadianencyclopedia.com/index.cfm?PgNm=TCE&Params=A1SEC826774|url-status=live |archive-date=November 21, 2009|title=Provincial Government in Canada |encyclopedia=[[The Canadian Encyclopedia]] |publisher=[[Historica Canada]] |first=Norman J. |last=Ruff |others=updated by Andrew McIntosh |date=30 October 2020}}</ref>  The premier is Prince Edward Island's [[head of government]], and the [[king of Canada]] is its [[head of state]] and is represented by the [[lieutenant governor of Prince Edward Island]].<ref>{{cite web|access-date=November 9, 2008|url=http://www.gov.pe.ca/lg/about.php3|title=The Office of Lieutenant Governor |publisher=Government of Prince Edward Island }}</ref> The premier picks a cabinet from the elected members to form the [[Executive Council of Prince Edward Island]], and presides over that body.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=November 9, 2008|url=http://www.gov.pe.ca/ec/index.php3|title=Executive Council |publisher=Government of Prince Edward Island }}</ref>

Members are first elected to the legislature during [[List of Prince Edward Island general elections|general elections]]. General elections must be conducted every five years from the date of the last election, but the premier may ask for early [[Dissolution of parliament#Canada|dissolution]] of the Legislative Assembly. An election may also take place if the governing party loses the confidence of the legislature by the defeat of a supply bill or tabling of a confidence motion.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=November 9, 2008|url=http://www.electionspei.ca/provincial/guide/|title=Guide to Provincial General Elections|publisher=Elections Prince Edward Island|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081017211727/http://www.electionspei.ca/provincial/guide/|archive-date=October 17, 2008|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}}</ref>

Prince Edward Island has had 46&nbsp;government leaders since it became a colony in 1851. The province had 7&nbsp;premiers while a colony and 34&nbsp;premiers after joining Confederation, of which 18<!--Pope was Premier both before and after Confederation--> were from the [[Prince Edward Island Progressive Conservative Party]] and 23 were from the [[Prince Edward Island Liberal Party]]. 

The current premier is [[Rob Lantz]], since February 9, 2026.
